extra.label: BIP-110 chain-split risk this weekend: block 961,632 activation height; miner signaling 2.6% (far below 55% threshold); replay attack vulnerability for holders
extra.value: Bitcoin BIP-110 (a controversial proposal to restrict non-payment data in Bitcoin transactions) has an activation height of approximately block 961,632, which may be reached this weekend. The proposal requires 55% miner signaling to enforce — as of Friday, signaling stood at approximately 2.6%, far below threshold. However, computers running BIP-110 software are programmed to reject non-signaling blocks once the activation height is reached, potentially creating a minority chain. Crypto.news reports that Bitcoin holders 'could lose real BTC through replay attacks if they sell coins created by a potential BIP-110 chain split without separating them.' Risk assessment: LOW probability of an actual minority chain forming (miner signaling 2.6% vs 55% required), but the activation height being reached this weekend creates weekend uncertainty and potential for low-liquidity price volatility. On-chain spot holders are not immediately at risk unless they transact during a chain-split window.

extra.label: BTCPay Server critical flaw (Aug 8): Lightning node credentials stolen; BTC funds at risk on LND nodes; on-chain wallets not affected — update to v2.4.2
extra.value: BTCPay Server disclosed a critical security vulnerability on August 8, 2026. Attackers exploited a flaw to steal 'macaroon' files — credentials granting full access to LND (Lightning Network Daemon) nodes. Affected operators reported funds being drained from their Lightning nodes. BTCPay confirmed the exploit and urgently advised all operators to update to version 2.4.2 or take servers offline immediately. Standard on-chain wallets generated within BTCPay are not affected. The attack was confirmed by hodlonaut on X: 'This is an ongoing attack on BTCPayserver users. Citadel21's lightning node was just swept.' The incident does not affect BTC spot holders transacting on-chain. However, it adds to a broader narrative of Bitcoin infrastructure vulnerability that may weigh on sentiment for Lightning Network payment adoption.
